stops.note: an Irish surname, from Ó Loingsigh or the Anglo-Norman Lynch family, one of the fourteen 'Tribes of Galway'
usually traced to Charles Lynch, a Virginia justice who ran extralegal courts punishing Loyalists in 1780, though Captain William Lynch of Pittsylvania County is a rival claimant
hardened into mob killing; the Tuskegee Institute recorded about 4,700 lynchings in the US between 1882 and 1968, most of them of Black Americans

current_meaning: (of a mob) to kill someone for an alleged offence without a legal trial
